title: Things I Have Loved: A collection (sort of)
body: A small red book of lists, letters and half-finished poems about the ordinary things one person couldn't stop loving. I read a page a night and it lasted me a whole winter.

trail.text: The list of kitchen sounds made me call my father.
Slow Arithmetic — https://example.com/slow-arithmetic

title: On mending things
body: Fixed the zip on a jacket I've had for eleven years instead of buying a new one. Took an hour. I feel more attached to it now than when it was new, as if the repair is part of the jacket.

trail.text: Same with a chipped bowl I glued back together. It's the only one I notice.

title: Thoreau, on the woods
body: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately. — Henry David Thoreau, Walden

trail.text: Taped this inside a kitchen cupboard.
Deliberately is the hard word.
the path I walk on Sundays

title: Kitchen Radio, 6 a.m.
body: An instrumental that sounds like someone making coffee very carefully so as not to wake the house. Plays well with rain.

title: Lentils for a grey Tuesday
body: Soften an onion in plenty of oil, add two crushed garlic cloves, a spoon of cumin, a cup of red lentils and three cups of water. Simmer twenty minutes. Finish with lemon and more oil than seems reasonable.

trail.text: Added a handful of spinach at the end. Good.
Smoked paprika instead of cumin works too.

title: Don't tell a soul
body: An invitation to a surprise party I never went to. I kept it for the handwriting.

title: The Verso Book of Feminism
body: Revolutionary words from four millennia of rebellion. Women, and people of any and no gender, protesting, theorising, writing manifestos, poems and songs, striking and fomenting revolution: from the female poets of the Tang Dynasty to the petroleuses of the Paris Commune to radical queer politics now. Open it anywhere.

trail.text: Start with the Trung sisters.

title: A rule I'm trying
body: Before I buy anything, I write down where it will live in the house. If I can't name the spot, I don't buy it.

title: Emerson, on the day
body: Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year. — Ralph Waldo Emerson

trail.text: Read this aloud at a friend's birthday dinner.

title: Bread, second attempt
body: A lopsided sourdough loaf on a wooden board, crust darker on one side. Better than the first.

trail.text: Mine looked exactly like this on attempt two. Attempt five is where it clicks.

title: Ferry Crossing (live)
body: A folk song recorded on an actual ferry; you can hear the engine and someone laughing at the end. Recommended with headphones and a window.

title: Burnt-honey figs
body: Halve figs, drizzle with honey, put under a hot grill until the honey just starts to burn. Serve with yoghurt and a pinch of salt.

trail.text: Plums work if you can't find figs.

title: Overheard on the bus
body: Two teenagers arguing seriously about whether clouds have weight. One of them won with a fact about elephants. I wrote it down so I wouldn't lose it.

trail.text: They do — a cumulus weighs about as much as a hundred elephants. Looked it up.
This made my whole commute.

title: Ex-Wife
body: It's 1924 and Peter and Patricia have a very modern marriage, until Peter doesn't, and Patricia starts over as a different kind of single woman. Published anonymously in 1929: speakeasies, morning-after aspirin, girl-talk and the freedoms and anguish of being alone. It reads like it was written last year.

title: Whitman, on contradiction
body: Do I contradict myself? Very well then I contradict myself. — Walt Whitman, Song of Myself

trail.text: My excuse for every changed mind.

title: Jewelry to Not be Missed
body: Excerpt from a girl who gave up wearing jewelry a long time ago.

title: What the piano teacher said
body: She said: play it slowly enough that you can't make a mistake, then play it slower than that. I've been applying it to everything.

trail.text: Tried this with handwriting. It works.
Gymnopédie No. 1, played very slowly — https://example.com/gymnopedie-slow

title: Laundromat Lullaby
body: A song built from the rhythm of a spin cycle. Strangely calming. Made by someone who clearly spent a lot of time waiting for washing.

title: Tomato toast, done properly
body: Good bread, toasted hard. Rub with a cut garlic clove, then a halved ripe tomato until only the skin is left in your hand. Salt, oil. That's it.

trail.text: Only worth it in August. Saving this for next summer.

title: Any Person Is the Only Self
body: Sixteen essays about a life lived alongside books: dog-eared and destroyed, cherished and discarded. Who are we when we read? When we journal? Are we more ourselves alone or with friends? Plath to Proust to hair metal and surf movies.

trail.text: The essay on rereading changed how I keep books.

title: Window seat, wool blanket
body: A window seat with a folded olive blanket, a mug ring on the sill, rain on the glass.

trail.text: I want to live in this photo.

title: Dickinson, on hope
body: Hope is the thing with feathers / That perches in the soul. — Emily Dickinson

trail.text: Sent this to my sister during a bad month.
a sparrow on our balcony rail

title: Letters I never sent
body: I keep a folder of letters I wrote and never sent. Reading them years later is like meeting an earlier version of myself who was braver and sillier.

title: Two Chairs on a Porch
body: A duet where the singers never quite finish each other's lines. Sounds like an old couple remembering a road trip slightly differently.

trail.text: Played this at my grandparents' anniversary.

title: Rice that fixes things
body: Rinse rice until the water runs clear. One part rice, one and a quarter water, a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, lid on, lowest heat for twelve minutes, then leave it alone for ten. Don't lift the lid. Don't.

title: Chalk on the pavement
body: A child's chalk drawing of a whale covering three paving stones, half washed away by rain.

title: Everything I Know About Love
body: Bad dates, good friends and, above all, realising you are enough. A memoir of your twenties in stories, lists and recipes, and a love letter to the best girlfriends who get you through all of it.

trail.text: Gave it to my sister. She gave it back with notes in the margins.

title: The ten-minute walk
body: When I'm stuck, I walk exactly ten minutes in one direction and ten minutes back. The answer is usually waiting at the turnaround point.

trail.text: Mine's a lap of the cemetery. Same effect.
Doing this tomorrow before the meeting.

title: Morris, on usefulness
body: Have nothing in your houses that you do not know to be useful, or believe to be beautiful. — William Morris

title: Rain on a Tin Roof (field recording)
body: Forty minutes of rain on a shed roof somewhere in the countryside. A crow comes in at minute twenty-three.

trail.text: Waited for the crow. Worth it.

title: Porridge, overnight
body: Oats, a pinch of salt, twice as much milk as oats, a grated apple. Leave in the fridge. Eat cold, standing up, while the kettle boils.

title: Stack of library returns
body: A trolley of returned library books, spines in every colour, one with a pressed flower sticking out.

trail.text: The pressed flower is the whole story.

title: How to Be Bored Well
body: A short, funny book arguing that boredom is a skill. Chapter titles include 'The Waiting Room as Monastery' and 'Staring Out of Windows, Professionally'.

title: The jar of good things
body: Every Friday I write one good thing from the week on a scrap of paper and put it in a jar. On New Year's Eve I read them all. Last year there were forty-one.

trail.text: Started one this week. One scrap so far: this note.

title: Austen, on books
body: I declare after all there is no enjoyment like reading! — Jane Austen, Pride and Prejudice

title: atelier Lin
body: Kept the card from a florist's studio long after the flowers had gone. The bent stem is the best part.

trail.text: The stem looks like it's bowing.

title: Whistling Down the Lane
body: Someone whistling an old tune while cycling, recorded on a phone. Slightly out of tune, completely happy.

title: Soup from what's left
body: Whatever vegetables are going soft, an onion, a stock cube, water to cover. Simmer until everything gives up. Blend half. Toast on the side, always.

trail.text: A spoon of miso at the end changes everything.

title: Things my neighbour grows on a balcony
body: Tomatoes, three kinds of mint, a lemon tree that has produced exactly one lemon, and a sunflower taller than the railing. She waters at 7 every evening and says hello to each one.

title: First frost on the car
body: Fern patterns of frost across a windscreen, sun just coming through behind them.

trail.text: Scraped mine this morning and felt bad about it after seeing this.
